seo.title: Knee Pain Treatment Melbourne | Alpha Sports Medicine
seo.description: Knee pain treatment in Melbourne with hands-on care and progressive rehabilitation. Understand what is driving your pain and build back capacity.

hero.heading: Knee pain does not have to mean stopping
hero.subheading: Knees respond to being loaded appropriately—not protected forever. We work out what is driving the pain and build back what your knee can tolerate.

urgent.heading: Some knee symptoms need medical assessment first
urgent.copy: Seek urgent care if you cannot bear weight, the knee is badly swollen or deformed after an injury, or it is hot and red and you have a fever. A knee that locks or repeatedly gives way should also be assessed promptly.

regions.title: Front of the knee
regions.copy: Pain around the kneecap is common in runners and active adults. It often appears when a recent increase in running, hills or gym work exceeds what the knee currently tolerates.

regions.title: Below the kneecap
regions.kicker: Jumping, landing or the morning after
regions.copy: A very localised sore spot in the tendon below the kneecap can behave like patellar tendinopathy. It usually needs carefully progressed loading rather than complete rest.

regions.title: Inside the knee
regions.kicker: Walking, twisting or getting out of the car
regions.copy: Pain along the inside joint line may relate to several structures, including an irritated meniscus, ligament or osteoarthritis. An assessment helps separate them.

regions.title: Outside the knee
regions.kicker: A consistent point during a run or ride
regions.copy: Outside knee pain is common in runners and cyclists. Training load and movement patterns are considered together rather than blaming one tight structure.

regions.title: Behind the knee
regions.copy: Tightness or fullness behind the knee can have several causes, including a Baker’s cyst. New or unexplained swelling should be assessed.

process.title: Start with your story
process.copy: What changed, what you have tried and what the knee has stopped you doing.

process.title: Assess the whole chain
process.copy: We examine the knee and how the hip, ankle and foot influence its workload.

process.title: Explain it clearly
process.copy: You leave understanding what we think is happening and what comes next.

process.title: Settle what is irritable
process.copy: Hands-on care may help symptoms while we introduce suitable movement.

process.title: Build capacity
process.copy: Progressive strength for the quadriceps, hips and calves is central for many presentations.

process.title: Return to your goal
process.copy: Running, stairs, squats, gardening or keeping up with the grandkids—the plan returns to real life.

faqs.question: Why does my knee hurt going down stairs?
faqs.answer: Going downstairs asks the front of the knee to manage a relatively high load. Pain can appear when that demand exceeds current capacity, particularly after changes in running, hills, gym work or time away from activity.

faqs.question: Why does my knee hurt after sitting?
faqs.answer: A sore or stiff knee after sitting is common with kneecap-related pain and osteoarthritis. The pattern is useful information, but it does not identify one diagnosis by itself.

faqs.question: Should I stop running with knee pain?
faqs.answer: Not always. Many people can temporarily adjust distance, hills, speed or frequency while building capacity. Sudden swelling, instability, locking or an inability to bear weight needs assessment first.

faqs.question: Are squats bad for my knees?
faqs.answer: Squatting is not automatically harmful. Range, load, technique and current tolerance all matter.

faqs.question: Do I need a scan?
faqs.answer: Many knee presentations can be assessed clinically first. Imaging may be useful after significant trauma, when serious injury is suspected, or when the result would change management.

faqs.question: Can exercise help knee osteoarthritis?
faqs.answer: Australian clinical guidance recommends individualised land-based exercise for knee osteoarthritis to improve pain and function.

faqs.question: Do I need a knee replacement?
faqs.answer: That decision belongs with you and your surgeon. Replacement can be effective for advanced osteoarthritis that has not responded to conservative care.

faqs.question: How long does knee rehabilitation take?
faqs.answer: Knee rehabilitation is usually measured in weeks to months, not days. The timeframe depends on the cause, duration, starting capacity and goal.

closing.heading: What have you stopped doing because of your knee?
closing.copy: Tell us what you want to get back to. We will assess the knee, explain the options and build the next step with you.
